A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeNOTS work and contain readable main text and complete Appendices A–C. Equations, figures, tables, and experiments can be matched despite restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results in Table 7, synthetic experiments, and forecasting, ablation, and robustness results throughout the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark scores in Table 11, and adds statistical performance ranks in Table 7.

M1.justification: Both versions use time rescaling, cubic-spline interpolation, GRU-based antisynchronous negative feedback, and a linear prediction head. The added discussion of disabling feedback explains the existing formulation without introducing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both retain UWGL, InsectSound, Pendulum, and Sepsis, together with Bump, SineMix, Sine-2, and regular/irregular Pendulum-Angles forecasting. No dataset, task, or input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmarks, vector-field studies, attacks, and forecasting experiments. Latent ODE already appears in v4 Table 14, corresponding to v5 Table 15; its added citation does not introduce a baseline.

E3.justification: v5 adds dataset-wise and mean performance ranks as evaluation summaries in Table 7. A rank counts statistically superior competitors plus one. The underlying preprocessing, training settings, model sizes, task metrics, and testing procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The time-scale/tolerance studies, forgetting experiments, reduced-data overfitting test, feedback-strength analysis, attack sweeps, and GP-assumption simulation are retained. Their relocation and renumbering do not introduce new ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: v5 adds one-sided t-tests with a p-value cutoff of 0.1 to construct Table 7 ranks. The earlier uncertainty-based highlighting remains in the relocated raw-results table. Reported run counts, seed information, and uncertainty-reporting practices otherwise remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v5 newly reports performance ranks, including mean ranks of 1.0 for DeNOTS and 1.25 for Sync-NF. Raw results remain unchanged: v4 Table 7 becomes v5 Table 11, retaining DeNOTS Pendulum 0.79 ± 0.02 and Sepsis 0.937 ± 0.005. The existing experimental curves and supplementary scores also match.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 changes from a Lipschitz upper bound to equality between classes of start-corrected ODE mappings, with new definitions, initial-state dependence, and a converse proof in Appendix B.1. Theorem 4.5 is reformulated around additive ODE perturbations and time-averaged error, extending beyond GP interpolation. The spline asymptotic, stability theorem, and forgetting theorem are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the discretization-error motivation to include numerical solvers, extending the scope of the non-accumulation claim. The principal time-scaling and feedback contributions, four-benchmark superiority claim, abstract, and conclusion otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets trajectory growth through numerical-integration-error accumulation and argues that stable feedback prevents this accumulation. v4 focused on uncertainty from input interpolation. The stated limitations, memory–robustness tradeoffs, and forecasting interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement changes the advertised anonymous repository from denots_neurips2025-7DE6 to denots_iclr2026-400E. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and compute disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether repository contents changed.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a focused discussion positioning time scaling against fixed, reparameterized, predicted, and invariant time treatments, citing additional work by Chen, Dupont, Rubanova, and Massaroli. Hairer and Reich support the numerical-error discussion; the Cohen randomized-smoothing citation is removed.

P1.justification: The theoretical exposition is substantially reorganized: Section 3 becomes definition-led, Section 4.2 separates integration and interpolation errors, and Appendix B separates general error propagation from GP interpolation. A new Full Results subsection accommodates the relocated benchmark table. Much of the experimental prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 introduces a rank table with a mean-rank column and moves the original main-results table into Appendix C.4. Several figures and tables are regrouped or relocated, but all 16 figures retain their graphical content and there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v5 provides more explicit theoretical exposition and statistical ranking while preserving the raw empirical evidence. However, its generalized robustness proof introduces a substantive inconsistency: Appendix B.4, Equation (16), multiplies the perturbation xi by a although the new Equation (7) adds xi outside that factor, affecting Theorem 4.5's bound. These presentation gains and unresolved theoretical correctness concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
